ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly high-intensity (white/light grey) internal surface area occupying approximately 75% of the visible fluke, contrasted against low-intensity (black/dark grey) perimeter boundaries and internal markings (~25%).
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Large contiguous white zone spanning the interior of both lobes. Low-intensity pigmentation is concentrated on the trailing edge boundary, distal tips, and localized linear/mottled clusters primarily distributed across the left lobe and the central convergence area.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Visible central V-shaped notch with a narrow vertex angle (approximately 35-45 degrees) and a clearly defined depth relative to the horizontal axis of the fluke.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency irregular serrations along the entire trailing edge boundary, with pixel-amplitude variations (peaks and valleys) of 3-10 pixels; serrations are more pronounced and jagged on the left lobe's trailing edge.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Convex mathematical curve extending from the median notch to the distal tips, with the right lobe exhibiting a slightly more elongated horizontal sweep compared to the left.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Detection of multiple circular, high-contrast white pixel clusters (~5-15 pixels in diameter) concentrated on the visible peduncle and the lower-central region where the fluke meets the body.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Presence of multiple dark, unaligned linear pixel streaks of varying lengths (10-60 pixels) and orientations, predominantly on the left fluke lobe, breaking the high-intensity white background.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Distinct circular indentation marks and raised white pigment clusters on the peduncle, consistent with historical parasitic or barnacle attachment sites.
other_distinctive_markers: Sharp, continuous black boundary line along the entire trailing edge and distal tips, providing a high-contrast transition against the internal white surface.
